categories.dairy: A2 milk is a great situational preference if you have digestive sensitivities, rather than just a trendy bio-hack.

foods.name: Apples
foods.meta: Doused with post-harvest chemicals; consistently on the EWG Dirty Dozen list.

foods.name: Pears
foods.meta: Thin skin retains high pesticide residues; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Peaches & Nectarines
foods.meta: Soft, porous skin absorbs pesticides easily; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Cherries
foods.meta: Thin skin retains heavy pesticide loads; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Bananas
foods.meta: Thick peel blocks pesticide transfer.

foods.name: Wild Blueberries
foods.meta: Contains 2x the antioxidant capacity of cultivated varieties.

foods.name: Cultivated Blueberries
foods.meta: Frequently test positive for toxic pesticides; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Strawberries & Blackberries
foods.meta: Porous structure retains heavy pesticide sprays; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Grapes
foods.meta: Thin skin easily absorbs pesticide sprays; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Watermelon
foods.meta: Thick rind acts as a natural barrier. Cheaper during the summer.
foods.appearance: Look for a creamy yellow spot, dull finish, and it should be heavy for its size.

foods.name: Cantaloupe & Honeydew
foods.meta: Thick outer rinds block pesticides; EWG Clean Fifteen.

foods.name: Avocados
foods.meta: Thick skin blocks pesticide transfer; EWG Clean Fifteen.

foods.name: Pineapple
foods.meta: Thick skin blocks pesticide transfer.
foods.appearance: Should smell sweet at the base, have a slight give, and be a golden color.

foods.name: Broccoli & Kale Sprouts
foods.meta: Microgreens have up to 40x the nutrient density of mature greens.

foods.name: Spinach
foods.meta: Highest pesticide residue by weight of all produce; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Kale & Collard Greens
foods.meta: Can carry up to 20 different pesticides; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Romaine & Leafy Lettuce
foods.meta: Large surface area catches chemical sprays.

foods.name: Potatoes
foods.meta: 90% of conventional carry post-harvest chemical sprout inhibitors; EWG Dirty Dozen.
foods.storage: Can often be stored for months in a cool, dark place.

foods.name: Sweet Potatoes
foods.meta: Directly absorb soil chemicals during growth.

foods.name: Carrots
foods.meta: Grown underground with low residue; EWG Clean Fifteen.
foods.storage: Can often be stored for months.

foods.name: Bell & Hot Peppers
foods.meta: Thin skin retains heavy pesticide loads; EWG Dirty Dozen.

foods.name: Onions
foods.meta: Sulfur compounds and underground bulbs resist pesticide buildup; EWG Clean Fifteen.
foods.storage: Can often be stored for months.

foods.name: Garlic
foods.meta: Sulfur compounds and underground bulbs resist pesticide buildup; EWG Clean Fifteen.

foods.name: Broccoli & Cauliflower
foods.meta: Minimal pesticide retention; EWG Clean Fifteen.

foods.name: Cabbage
foods.meta: Protective outer leaves limit chemical absorption; EWG Clean Fifteen.

foods.name: Eggs
foods.meta: Deep orange yolks; outdoor foraging boosts omega-3s and lutein.
foods.avoid: "Cage-Free" & "Vegetarian-Fed" (birds remain crammed indoors on soy/corn feed).

foods.name: Beef
foods.meta: 5x the omega-3s, higher CLA, and robust antioxidants.
foods.avoid: Plain "Grass-Fed" (animals are still fattened on feedlot grain during final months).

foods.name: Poultry
foods.meta: Outdoor foraging optimizes healthy fat ratios and vitamin E.
foods.avoid: "Free-Range" & "Natural" (often means minimal access to a small outdoor porch).

foods.name: Salmon
foods.meta: Rich in natural astaxanthin antioxidants and clean omega-3s.
foods.avoid: "Farm-Raised" / "Atlantic" (higher PCB contaminants and synthetic color additives).

foods.name: Shrimp
foods.meta: Cleaner ocean sourcing.
foods.avoid: Imported Farmed (notorious for heavy antibiotic use in farm water).

foods.name: Milk & Cream
foods.meta: Preserves vital vitamin K2 and fat-soluble vitamins.
foods.avoid: "Skim / Fat-Free" (strips away essential fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K).

foods.name: Butter
foods.meta: Significantly higher omega-3s and CLA content.

foods.name: White Rice
foods.meta: Generally lower in naturally occurring arsenic than brown rice.

foods.name: Brown Rice
foods.avoid: Contains higher levels of arsenic than white rice.
foods.storage: Contains more natural oils and goes rancid much sooner than white rice.
